deck.title: BC Ferries Project Coordinator
deck.description: Interview preparation for capital and operational project coordination in a marine transportation environment.

cards.question: Tell us about a complex project you coordinated with multiple stakeholders and tight deadlines.
answerFramework: Scope, timeline, and why coordination mattered
Tools and rituals (status meetings, RAID log, milestones)
How you handled a surprise constraint

star.situation: Multi-vendor or cross-department initiative affecting terminal operations.
star.task: Keep schedule, budget visibility, and communications aligned.
star.action: Built integrated plan, tracked risks, escalated early on slip.
star.result: Delivered on time or with agreed change control; stakeholders informed throughout.

cards.bestStory: Terminal upgrade or vessel-related project where downtime had revenue impact—you coordinated trades, IT, and operations.
watchFor: Taking sole credit for team outcomes
No mention of documentation or follow-through

whatGoodSoundsLike: Calm coordinator who connects technical and business views

cards.question: How would you handle a supplier delay that threatens a critical project milestone?
answerFramework: Assess impact on critical path and operations
Options: alternate supplier, scope swap, schedule recovery
Escalation path and communication to sponsors

star.situation: Key equipment delivery slip on refit or terminal project.
star.task: Protect milestone without hiding bad news.
star.action: Quantified delay, proposed mitigation, negotiated partial delivery or re-sequence.
star.result: Minimized operational impact; execs had decision-ready options.

cards.bestStory: Supplier missed steel or electrical lead time—you re-sequenced work packages and kept crews productive.

whatGoodSoundsLike: Understands cost of schedule slip in ferry context
